one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent assumed the binary's output could be reproduced by simple 2D gradient and checkerboard math without recognizing it was a ray tracer, producing fundamentally wrong implementations that never matched despite 90 steps of heuristic tweaking.
t_err_evidence: Agent creates mystery.c with hardcoded row-based gradient instead of actual ray-tracing logic.
t_commit_evidence: Step 24: Once the wrong algorithmic approach was written, all subsequent steps (37 on) iterate on heuristic tweaks to this same wrong approach (mystery_final.c, mystery_correct.c, mystery_exact.c) with no attempt to implement actual ray tracing; the outcome was locked in from the first implementation.
t_surface_evidence: MD5 sums differ: reimplementation a69002cc vs original e866fa2c, confirming output mismatch.
trigger_explanation: The agent analyzed output pixels (gradient sky + alternating checkerboard ground) and assumed these could be reproduced by simple 2D per-pixel formulas, never considering that the distinct pixel pattern variations across both X and Y axes (sub-pixel diagonal patterns, perspective-projected ground checkerboard) indicate ray-traced geometry. This unverified assumption about algorithm structure drove the entire implementation.
